 TNN Updated: Nov 12, 2026, 10:10 IST Telangana is set to replace its existing Intermediate education system with a unified 10+2 structure from the 2027-28 academic year. Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy has directed officials to prepare for the transition, bringing classes XI and XII under the school education framework.
 Under the proposed structure, school education will be divided into three stages: primary education from kindergarten to class IV, secondary education from classes V to VIII, and senior secondary education from classes IX to XII. The move will effectively integrate the two years of Intermediate education into the school system, replacing the existing arrangement in which students move to separate junior colleges after completing class X.
 The government has proposed giving special attention to classes IX to XII as a distinct phase of learning, with greater emphasis on specialised education, language proficiency and communication skills. Adequate classrooms, laboratories, teaching facilities and other academic resources will be essential to facilitating the transition.
 Currently, school education up to class X is administered by the School Education Department and culminates in the Secondary School Certificate (SSC) examination conducted by the Board of Secondary Education. 
 Intermediate education for classes XI and XII is governed separately by the Telangana Board of Intermediate Education, with students generally enrolling in junior colleges after completing their SSC examinations.
 The proposed reform will bring the two stages under a unified school education framework. The transition is expected to require administrative restructuring, infrastructure upgrades, and arrangements for the availability of qualified teachers.
 The government has also emphasised strengthening government schools to provide facilities and academic standards comparable to private institutions. The state government has also underlined the importance of skill development and employment-oriented learning as part of its broader education vision.
